rationale: Two independent double-blind randomized controlled trials of coated cantaloupe juice concentrate (Extramel 10 mg/d) in stressed healthy adults reported statistically significant improvements in selective attention and cognitive performance: Carillon et al. (2014, n=61) showed Stroop/reverse-Stroop attention gains of +13.9% at day 28 (p<0.04) and +20.8% at day 84 (p<0.001) vs placebo, corroborated by Milesi et al. (2009, n=70) showing improved FARD Cognitive pole (p=0.032) and a concentration trend (p=0.091). Because both trials used proprietary coated concentrate in non-PD stressed adults (and sponsor funding applies), this yields a minimal directional signal (Maybe True, 50.005) consistent with Round 1 cantaloupe fatigue precedent.

No controlled human study or Parkinson animal model tests whether raw cantaloupe worsens bradykinesia severity. Existing melon trials used proprietary coated melon SOD concentrates (Extramel/GliSODin) in non-PD adults without PD motor outcomes (Koike 2022 null; Milesi 2009 and Carillon 2014 lacked motor endpoints), Hegelmaier 2020 bundled melon into a multi-food PD vegetarian menu, and preclinical rotarod screens tested non-flesh seeds or peels (Sayyar 2023; Dokkada 2025).

No clinical trial tests whether raw cantaloupe worsens or eases constipation in Parkinson's disease. Prokinetic rodent laxative findings (Gao et al., 2012) used rectal extracts of the bitter non-edible muskmelon stalk (Pedicellus Melo), not oral raw cantaloupe flesh, and a human crossover of unripe Apulian melon (Khalil et al., 2025) did not measure constipation. Public Parkinson's UK forum discussions preserve mixed lived experience: one contributor favored melon as a soluble-fiber fruit alongside warm water, while another warned fruit intake alone failed to prevent severe colonic obstruction.

Maybe False (50.005): Contrary to the frozen claim that roasted chicken worsens anxiety, two independent double-blind human RCTs of aqueous chicken soup or Essence of Chicken reported modest reductions in subjective tension/anxiety—Midoh & Noguchi 2009 (n=30 crossover, lower POMS Tension-Anxiety vs placebo, p<0.05) and Young, Benton & Carter 2015 (n=46 completers, lower VAS Anxious/Composed ratings, p<0.04, though GHQ-Anxiety was null)—bridged to thermally cooked chicken breast histidine dipeptides (carnosine/anserine) by Kouriki-Nagatomo 2019. Signal remains minimal because a larger hydrolyzed chicken extract RCT was null on STAI-State (p=0.354) and STAI-Trait (p=0.342) anxiety (Wu 2020, n=73), dry-heat roasting differs from aqueous chicken broth/extract, and no Parkinson's anxiety trial exists.

Maybe False (51): Contrary to the frozen claim that poached chicken reduces daily OFF time, four controlled Parkinson's disease dietary protein/LNAA clinical trials (Barichella 2006 n=18; Tsui 1989 n=10; Carter 1989 n=5; Eriksson 1988) establish that high daytime dietary protein and large neutral amino acids (LNAAs) compete with levodopa for intestinal and blood-brain-barrier transport and WORSEN daily OFF time. This clinical mechanism bridges directly to poached chicken via a human meal crossover showing cooked chicken produces rapid postprandial rises in plasma essential/LNAA concentrations (r=0.90, faster than fish, p<0.05; Uhe 1992) and compositional confirmation of ~22.5 g high-LNAA protein per 110 g steamed chicken breast (Uchida 2024; Li 2021). Effect is moderated by individual sensitivity (~12-20% overall prevalence, higher in advanced fluctuating PD; Virmani 2016), normal-diet fluctuation nuances (Nutt 1989), and proper meal-medication spacing (Cucca 2015).

In the controlled VA IC/BPS cohort (Jarman 2023), chicken was simply non-bothersome (2% IC/BPS, 0% controls)—a neutral tolerability profile rather than active urgency relief.

Maybe False (51): Contrary to the frozen claim that baked cod reduces daily OFF time, four controlled Parkinson's disease protein/LNAA clinical trials (Barichella 2006 n=18; Tsui 1989 n=10; Carter 1989 n=5; Eriksson 1988) establish that daytime dietary protein and large neutral amino acids (LNAAs) compete with levodopa transport and WORSEN daily OFF time. This mechanism bridges directly to baked Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) fillet via HPLC amino acid profiling confirming high lean protein density and abundant competing LNAAs (Quaresma 2023), a human 250 g cod fillet meal study (43 g protein) demonstrating substantial postprandial plasma amino acid elevations (Soucy & Leblanc 1999, n=10), and a human meal crossover verifying fish protein elevates plasma essential/LNAAs (r=0.90, peaking more slowly than beef/chicken, p<0.05; Uhe 1992). Effect is tempered by patient-level sensitivity (~12-20% overall, higher in advanced fluctuating PD; Virmani 2016), normal-diet nuances (Nutt 1989), chronic fasting BCAA dynamics (Schmedes 2018), and meal-medication spacing (Cucca 2015).

In the prospective Seniors-ENRICA-1 cohort (Carballo-Casla 2022, n=950 older adults), oily fish was associated with reduced pain worsening whereas WHITE fish (lean cod-type fish) was explicitly NULL for pain. Human cod-protein feeding trials measured only systemic inflammatory biomarkers—hs-CRP reduction (Ouellet 2008, n=19) and serum neopterin (Helland 2021, NCT02350595) and urinary oxidative stress (Parra 2007)—without clinical pain outcomes; Mendelian randomization linked non-oily fish to higher serum uric acid (Ou 2024) without clinical gouty pain; and Parkinson's UK forum discussions (Thread 4189) reflect cod liver oil capsules rather than lean grilled cod fillet.

Unknown (Researched): No controlled trial has tested whether grilled Atlantic cod fillet alters postural instability in Parkinson's disease. In older adults, 12 months of Atlantic cod protein hydrolysate showed null Short Physical Performance Battery balance/mobility scores (Nygard 2021, p=0.41).

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial, observational study, or experimental model has tested whether baked Atlantic cod fillet improves hypomimia or reduced facial expressiveness in Parkinson's disease.

Unknown (Researched): No controlled trial or observational study has linked baked Atlantic cod fillet to worsened Parkinson's rest tremor. Population-based Faroese meat/seafood tremor data (Ferrer & Louis 2020) showed no dietary meat/fish association with tremor or blood harmane after correction, and baked cod has low mercury levels (Dahl 2020).

Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial has tested whether poached Atlantic cod fillet improves Parkinson's stride length. In older adults, 12 months of cod protein hydrolysate showed null gait speed and SPPB (Nygard 2021, p=0.41) without measuring stride length.
Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial or observational study has tested whether poached Atlantic cod fillet worsens speech intelligibility or dysarthria in Parkinson's disease.

Unknown (Researched): No controlled videofluoroscopic or clinical dysphagia trial has tested whether boneless poached Atlantic cod fillet reduces swallowing difficulty in Parkinson's disease. Tablet-swallowing difficulty in the 12-month older-adult cod hydrolysate trial was null (Nygard 2021, p=0.11), emergency choking series highlight mechanical FISH-BONE foreign bodies (67% of choking admissions in Saccomanno 2023, n=138) rather than boneless poached fillet physiology, and Parkinson's UK forum members mention flaky moist fish only as an informal soft-texture meal preference.

Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial or urology cohort links poached Atlantic cod fillet to worsened urinary urgency frequency. In the nationwide VA IC/BPS food-sensitivity cohort (Jarman 2023, N=425), non-spicy lean meats/fish (e.g., tuna 2% IC/BPS, 1% HC) were among the least bothersome items with no cohort difference (p>0.05), and the OAB bladder-irritants review (Ha 2025) does not implicate lean white fish.
Unknown (Researched): No clinical trial, observational cohort, or experimental model has tested whether poached Atlantic cod fillet reduces visual hallucinations or Parkinson's disease psychosis.

Unknown (Researched): Controlled human cod-protein and white-fish aging studies show NULL effects on walking speed and mobility, and no trial tests poached Atlantic cod fillet on Parkinson's gait velocity. In community-dwelling older adults, 12 months of daily Atlantic cod fillet hydrolysate (Nygard 2021, n=86) was null on Short Physical Performance Battery (p=0.41) and walking speed, NCT02045355 terminated without posted mobility results, and Seniors-ENRICA found white fish null on functional impairment (Garcia-Esquinas 2019).

Maybe False (minimal_signal toward worsening): controlled human trials and three meta-analyses demonstrate that caffeine and brewed coffee acutely increase anxiety and jitteriness—especially at >200 mg or in low-habitual consumers and ADORA2A rs5751876 TT carriers (Rogers 2010 n=379; Haskell-Ramsay 2018 n=59 brewed coffee crossover; Ramirez-delaCruz 2024 n=29; Zhang 2026 15-RCT MA SMD 0.51; Liu 2024 MA SMD 0.94; Klevebrant 2022 MA). Tempered by null PD anxiety contrasts in Postuma 2012 (n=61), Postuma 2017 (n=118), Sauerbier 2018 (n=139), and Gabbert 2023 (n=4,914) and lower BAI at 400 mg/d in OAB women (Staack 2022), keeping evidence at minimal_signal.

Unknown (Researched): no randomized trial evaluates brewed coffee or caffeine on Parkinson's apathy severity; observational PD data conflict (Cho 2018 cross-sectional de novo PD n=196 linked coffee drinking to lower lack-of-motivation prevalence, whereas Sauerbier 2018 n=139 found null NMSS mood/apathy), and a controlled fatigue trial (Ataka 2008 n=18) found caffeine had no effect on subjective motivation.

Maybe True (limited_clinical_link toward easing): a direct Parkinson's crossover trial after 7-day caffeine washout (Sharma 2022, n=24 PD + 42 older controls, 100 mg caffeine in decaf coffee vs decaf coffee) significantly reduced choice-reaction-time errors (p=0.049), improved Stroop accuracy (p=0.018), speeded Stroop RT in PD (p=0.049), and improved dual-item RSVP accuracy (p=0.037), while paradoxically impairing single-item RSVP (p=0.044). Direct brewed-coffee crossovers outside PD (Haskell-Ramsay 2018 n=59; Han 2020 n=49; Hindmarch 1998/2000) corroborate acute vigilance/attention gains, tempered by Café-PD global MoCA (-0.66 pts, not isolated to attention) and Akyurek 2024 null RSVP.

Unknown (Researched): no human clinical trial evaluates decaffeinated coffee on Parkinson's bradykinesia severity; isolated caffeine PD motor trials (Postuma 2012/2017) cannot transfer to decaffeinated coffee, UK Biobank (Zhang 2024) found decaf null for PD risk, and preclinical EHT studies (Lee 2011; Yan 2018) show non-caffeine constituents require synergy or supraphysiologic dosing.

Maybe True (minimal_signal toward easing): randomized surgical and colonic-manometry trials directly testing decaffeinated coffee against water show accelerated bowel recovery and colonic motility—Dulskas 2015 (n=90 colectomy RCT: decaf first bowel movement 3.00 vs 4.14 d water, p<0.05), Rao 1998 (n=12 crossover: decaf increased colonic pressure waves p<0.01 and propagated contractions p<0.05), Brown 1990 (n=14: decaf increased rectosigmoid motility p<0.05 in responders), and Watanabe 2021 MA (13 RCTs showing no difference between caffeinated and decaf coffee). Tempered by a null colectomy RCT (Nasseri 2023, n=99, p=0.53), null NHANES decaf constipation association (Kong 2024, n=7,844), and absence of PD trials.

Maybe False (minimal_signal toward easing): in a double-blind Parkinson's crossover study (Deleu 2006, n=12), oral caffeine before levodopa shortened levodopa Tmax and shortened latency to onset of walking and finger-tapping motor response—easing acute delayed-ON latency rather than worsening OFF time. However, Deleu 2006 tested isolated caffeine capsules on single-dose onset latency rather than 24-hour diary OFF time, Moccia 2016 (n=79 PD 4-yr) found null UPDRS-IV complications, and Café-PD (Postuma 2017, n=118) showed increased dyskinesia without isolated OFF-time gains, capping confidence at minimal_signal.

Maybe False (limited_clinical_link toward easing): two multicenter double-blind PD RCTs of isolated caffeine—bridged to brewed coffee via Haskell-Ramsay 2018 (100 mg/220 mL) and Jeon 2019 HPLC—demonstrate modest short-to-medium-term easing of PD daytime sleepiness: Postuma 2012 (n=61 somnolent PD: CGI-C +0.64, PP ESS -1.97, ITT ESS -1.71) and Café-PD (Postuma 2017, n=118: 6-mo MDS-UPDRS 1.8 -0.49 [-0.79 to -0.20], 3-mo SCOPA-sleep daytime -1.09 [-1.88 to -0.30], attenuating by 12-18 mo). Direct brewed-coffee crossovers outside PD (Haskell-Ramsay 2018 n=59 alertness p<0.0005; Hindmarch 1998/2000) corroborate acute anti-somnolence, while PD espresso n-of-1 trials (Ferreira 2016 n=4) were mixed.

Unknown (Researched): neither cohort data nor controlled coffee trials show that regular decaffeinated coffee reduces depressive symptom severity—the Nurses' Health Study (Lucas 2011, n=50,739) found decaffeinated coffee completely null for depression risk while caffeinated coffee was inverse, and Haskell-Ramsay 2018 (n=59) found regular brewed decaf did not significantly improve overall mood over placebo.

Unknown (Researched): no controlled study tests brewed coffee or caffeine on dream enactment frequency in Parkinson's disease or RBD; in a cross-sectional survey of 96 polysomnography-confirmed iRBD patients (Jun 2022), 26.0% (25/96) perceived caffeine as an aggravating factor and 74% reported no aggravation, while Arnaldi 2017 notes caffeine is not protective against iRBD.

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial evaluates brewed coffee on Parkinson's drooling severity; Fox Insight PD survey data (Gabbert 2023, n=4,892) showed no significant association between coffee drinking (p=0.0823) or weekly dosage (p=0.9754) and saliva/drooling, and a controlled crossover outside PD (Hildebrandt 2013, n=35) found caffeinated drinks did not alter salivary flow.

Maybe False (limited_clinical_link toward worsening): in the multicenter double-blind Café-PD trial (Postuma 2017, n=118 analyzed PD, caffeine 200 mg BID vs placebo, bridged to brewed coffee via Haskell-Ramsay 2018 and Jeon 2019 HPLC), caffeine modestly worsened MDS-UPDRS 4.1+4.2 dyskinesia scores across combined visits (+0.25 pts, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.45; +0.36 [0.02 to 0.70] at 18 mo), corroborated by historical clinical challenge data (Shoulson & Chase 1975, n=6 PD) showing prolonged levodopa dyskinesia duration. Tempered by null 6-week dyskinesia in Postuma 2012 (n=61, only 14 with baseline dyskinesia) and observational CALM-PD data (Wills 2013, HR 0.61 [0.37-1.01]).

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial, observational cohort, or preclinical model evaluates decaffeinated coffee on Parkinson's dystonia severity; existing caffeine/coffee PD studies do not isolate decaffeinated coffee or dystonia endpoints.

Unknown (Researched): clinical evidence on brewed coffee or caffeine for pure executive function is null or conflicting—Sharma 2022 (n=24 PD + 42 controls) explicitly found NO selective Stroop interference/inhibition effect (F<1), Todorovic 2021 (n=16) found caffeine alone null on TMT-A/B, Café-PD (Postuma 2017, n=118 PD) reported slightly worse global MoCA (-0.66 pts, not isolated to executive function), and observational cohorts conflict (Cornelis 2020 UKB worse TMT-B vs Zhang 2026 JAMA better global TICS).

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial or cohort tracks fall frequency under decaffeinated coffee in Parkinson's disease or older adults; a 4-arm older-adult crossover (Richardson 2024, n=22) found decaffeinated coffee had no effect on standing postural control or Senior Fitness Test performance.

Maybe True (minimal_signal toward easing): Kitagawa 2007 evaluated oral caffeine 100 mg/day—equivalent to ~1 cup of brewed coffee (Haskell-Ramsay 2018; Jeon 2019)—in people with Parkinson's disease and freezing of gait (FOG), reporting improvement in the 'total akinesia' FOG subtype (no benefit in 'trembling in place') with tolerance restored after a 2-week washout. Because Kitagawa 2007 was uncontrolled with exact sample size and quantitative FOG scores missing from the indexed abstract (reliability_fit=remote), while Gabbert 2023 (n=4,889 PD) showed null coffee-freezing association (p=0.2364) and Postuma 2012/2017 did not isolate FOG, evidence stays at minimal_signal.

Unknown (Researched): the largest double-blind RCT directly testing brewed coffee on fine manual dexterity (Gerdes 2022, n=107 surgeons, 340 mL caffeinated vs decaf coffee) found completely null effects (p=0.079 and p=0.511), and Fuller 2021 found overall nine-hole peg test performance null (gain only in post-hoc high-fatigue subgroup). While acute caffeine sped finger-tapping latency in PD (Deleu 2006 n=12) and healthy adults (Fagan 1988 n=18), some PD patients report coffee-induced hand shaking (Parkinson's UK 2024), leaving net hand dexterity open.

Maybe False (minimal_signal toward worsening): randomized trials directly testing brewed caffeinated coffee show clear nighttime sleep disruption—the NEJM CRAVE randomized case-crossover (Marcus 2023, n=100) showed caffeinated coffee cut nightly sleep by 36 minutes (397 vs 432 min, 95% CI -47 to -25), and Hindmarch 2000 (n=30 brewed coffee crossover) worsened LSEQ sleep onset, duration, and quality (p<0.001)—corroborated by caffeine-timing sleep RCTs (Drake 2013; Gardiner 2025; Pauchon 2024). In PD, Café-PD (Postuma 2017, n=118) showed small non-significant nighttime sleep worsening (CIs crossing zero) while morning-only dosing (Postuma 2012 PSQI; Staack 2022 ISI) was null, keeping evidence at minimal_signal.
Unknown (Researched): no human clinical trial, cohort, or acoustic study evaluates decaffeinated coffee on low voice volume (hypophonia) in Parkinson's disease.

Maybe True (limited_clinical_link toward easing): in Postuma 2012 (n=61 PD, 6-week double-blind RCT of oral caffeine 100-200 mg BID vs placebo, bridged to brewed coffee via Haskell-Ramsay 2018 and Jeon 2019 HPLC), caffeine significantly reduced the UPDRS Part III rigidity subcomponent by -1.01 points (95% CI -2.0 to -0.7) alongside total UPDRS III (-3.15, -5.50 to -0.83), matching Round 2 black tea precedent 0631. Tempered by the larger 6-18 month Café-PD trial (Postuma 2017, n=118 analyzed PD) showing null total MDS-UPDRS III (-0.48, -3.21 to 2.25; rigidity subscore not isolated), suggesting possible tachyphylaxis.

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial evaluates decaffeinated coffee on Parkinson's olfactory impairment; in a crossover trial in healthy adults (Han 2020, n=49), acute olfactory threshold, discrimination, and identification did not differ between caffeinated and decaffeinated coffee, and no study compares decaffeinated coffee against a non-coffee control for hyposmia.

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial measures orthostatic lightheadedness symptoms after decaffeinated coffee in Parkinson's disease; controlled hemodynamic studies outside PD show decaffeinated coffee generally has null acute blood-pressure effects compared with water or regular coffee (Nussberger 1990; Lima de Castro 2024; Aoun 2021 intradialytic hypotension 26% vs 27%, p=0.539) and fails to replicate caffeine's pressor prevention of postprandial hypotension (Heseltine 1991), while Corti 2002 saw supine BP/MSNA elevation only in 9 non-habitual drinkers.

Unknown (Researched): ordinary decaffeinated coffee shows null analgesic effects across controlled non-PD trials—Haskell-Ramsay 2018 (n=59) found regular brewed coffee reduced headache versus decaf (p=0.0049) and placebo (p=0.015) while decaf was null vs placebo, Aoun 2021 (n=139) found dialysis headache identical between regular and decaf (p=0.522), and switching habitual drinkers to decaf provoked withdrawal headache (van Dusseldorp 1990). Camfield 2013 (n=60) reduced acute headache only with a specialized chlorogenic-acid-enriched green-roasted decaf blend, leaving ordinary decaffeinated coffee for PD pain open.

Unknown (Researched): two non-PD balance crossovers conflict—a better-controlled 4-arm crossover in older adults (Richardson 2024, n=22, mean age 68 y) found decaffeinated coffee had NO effect on standing center-of-pressure postural control versus matched placebo or no-fluid control (p>0.05), whereas a smaller unstandardized trial in young adults (Cildir 2021, n=15 in decaf arm, milk/sugar allowed, after 48-h caffeine abstention) saw lower before-after SOT composite/C5 scores (p=0.001). No PD balance trial exists, leaving the claim open.
Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial, observational cohort, or preclinical study evaluates decaffeinated coffee on reduced facial expressiveness (hypomimia) in Parkinson's disease.

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial evaluates decaffeinated coffee versus a non-coffee control on Parkinson's rest tremor severity; isolated caffeine tremor trials cannot transfer to decaffeinated coffee, UK Biobank (Zhang 2024) found decaf null for PD incidence, and PD forum discussions mention switching to decaf merely to avoid caffeinated coffee's tremor-worsening effect rather than showing intrinsic rest-tremor relief.

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial measures stride length under brewed coffee or caffeine in Parkinson's disease or older adults; Postuma 2012 reported non-significant general UPDRS gait items (CIs spanning zero) without measuring stride length, and CRAVE (Marcus 2023, n=100) measured daily step count (+1,058 steps/d) rather than spatial stride length.
Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial, observational cohort, or kinematic handwriting study evaluates brewed coffee or caffeine on Parkinson's micrographia (small handwriting severity).

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial tests brewed coffee on speech intelligibility in Parkinson's disease; Fox Insight PD survey data (Gabbert 2023, n=4,892) showed no significant association between coffee drinking (p=0.1615) or weekly dosage (p=0.7086) and speech problems.

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial evaluates brewed coffee on oropharyngeal dysphagia in Parkinson's disease; Fox Insight (Gabbert 2023, n=4,892) showed a marginal binary inverse link (p=0.0497) with completely null dosage (p=0.6961) and duration (p=0.4785) trends—consistent with reverse causation from dysphagia reducing beverage intake (Cassani 2017)—while Lohsiriwat 2006 (n=12 healthy) measured lower esophageal sphincter relaxation rather than oropharyngeal swallowing.

Maybe True (minimal_signal toward worsening): two controlled non-PD bladder trials—bridged to brewed coffee via Jeon 2019 HPLC and matching Round 2 black tea precedent 0641—show caffeinated beverages worsen urinary urgency: Wells 2014 (n=11 completed OAB women DB crossover) found decaffeinated vs caffeinated drinks reduced urgency (p<0.01), frequency (p<0.05), and ICIQ-OAB (p<0.01), and Bryant 2002 (n=95 continence patients RCT) showed caffeine reduction improved urgency (p=0.002) and frequency (p=0.037), supported by Gleason 2013 (NHANES n=4,309) and Park 2023 review. Tempered by Swithinbank 2005 (n=69 null), Ha 2025 mixed review, and Sauerbier 2018 null PD NMSS urinary domain.

Unknown (Researched): no clinical trial evaluates brewed coffee on visual hallucination frequency in Parkinson's disease; controlled and survey studies outside PD found null links between caffeine/coffee and hallucination-like experiences (Agoston 2022 DB RCT n=181; Agoston 2018 n=2,259), and Sauerbier 2018 (n=139 PD) showed null NMSS perceptual/hallucination scores.

Maybe False (minimal_signal toward easing): in a double-blind PD crossover (Deleu 2006, n=12), caffeine before levodopa shortened latency to walking response and increased walking response magnitude, corroborated by controlled older-adult gait-speed trials of caffeine (Marinho 2024, n=15: faster 10-m walk p=0.008 & TUG p=0.002; Waer 2024, n=85: faster 10-m walk p<0.05). Tempered by null walking speed in Norager 2005 (n=30 >=70 y), null Senior Fitness Test under brewed coffee in Richardson 2024 (n=22 older adults), null general UPDRS gait in Postuma 2012, and missing quantitative walking-speed CIs in Deleu 2006's abstract, capping confidence at minimal_signal.

No human clinical trials, PD observational cohorts, or preclinical Parkinson's models test steamed collard greens (Brassica oleracea var. viridis) for anxiety severity. Analytical studies prove broccoli sulforaphane findings cannot be transferred to collards: edible collard leaves contain low total glucosinolates (2.64 umol/g DW) with no detectable leaf glucoraphanin (Đulović 2023, PMC9965355), marked cultivar variability down to 1.0% glucoraphanin (Lee 2017, PMC5612653), progoitrin content (Felker 2016), and thermal myrosinase inactivation/leaching during cooking (Song & Thornalley 2007). Local NCT05532358 mentions collards only in vitamin K exclusion criteria. Southern US (Yang 2013), East African sukuma wiki (Ikuomola 2025), and Mediterranean domestication (Mabry 2021) records provide cultural dietary context only, leaving anxiety severity Unknown (Researched).

Evidence for cooked collard greens (Brassica oleracea var. viridis) affecting attention impairment is Unknown (Researched). Although the prospective Rush Memory and Aging Project cohort (Morris et al. 2018, PMID:29263222, PMC5772164; n=960 older adults) found slower cognitive decline with higher green leafy vegetable consumption, its FFQ pooled spinach, kale/collards/greens, and lettuce together and cannot isolate collard greens alone (exposure_fit: unusable). Furthermore, analytical chemistry refutes borrowing broccoli sulforaphane signals for collards: Đulović et al. 2023 (PMC9965355) found only 2.64 umol/g DW total glucosinolates in edible collard leaves with NO detectable leaf glucoraphanin, Lee et al. 2017 (PMC5612653) documented extreme cultivar variation (as low as 1.0% glucoraphanin), and Song & Thornalley 2007 (PMID:17011103) showed boiling leaches ~90% of Brassica glucosinolates and inactivates myrosinase. Human bioavailability studies confirm collard phylloquinone (Erkkilä 2004; Ellis 2019), lutein (Lienau 2003), and alpha-tocopherol (Traber 2015) absorption without cognitive trials.

Human and preclinical coriander SEED studies provide a consistent anxiolytic signal: Alqudah et al. 2024 (DOI 10.1108/nfs-08-2023-0193 / local NCT05999071; n=86 university students) found 500 mg dried powdered Coriandrum sativum seeds twice daily for 30 days significantly improved Hospital Anxiety Scale scores versus placebo (P=0.04), reinforced by two independent mouse seed-extract experiments—Mahendra & Bisht 2011 (PMID:22022003, PMC3195130; oral fruit/seed extract 100-200 mg/kg anxiolytic across 4 models) and Emamghoreishi et al. 2005 (PMID:15619553; aqueous seed extract 100 mg/kg i.p. anxiolytic on EPM)—plus Persian traditional calming use (Sobhani 2022). Because Alqudah 2024 enrolled healthy young students (non-PD), was retrospectively registered, and omitted arm-level means/CIs in the abstract, certainty is graded minimal_signal (50.005).

No human clinical trials, PD cohorts, or targeted animal models test ground coriander seed (Coriandrum sativum fruit/seed) for apathy severity in Parkinson's disease. Verified seed-specific research focuses on migraine pain (Delavar Kasmaei 2016), student anxiety/depression/sleep/memory (Alqudah 2024), MPTP mouse open-field/rotarod rescue (Koppula 2021), roasting volatile/lipid retention (Zhang 2015; Serag 2019; local Elmassry 2018), and multi-spice metabolic registries (local PolySPice NCT02599272), none of which directly evaluate apathy severity. Coriander LEAF (cilantro) studies (e.g., Lee 2026; Saeki 2022) are strictly separated from seed claims, and Persian/Ayurvedic/Sri Lankan ethnobotany (Sobhani 2022; local Otoom 2006) provides traditional context only, leaving apathy severity Unknown (Researched).

Evidence for toasted coriander seed affecting attention impairment is Unknown (Researched). While Alqudah et al. 2024 (n=86 students, powdered seed) reported improved self-reported prospective/retrospective memory (PRMQ, P=0.006), Koppula 2021 improved passive avoidance in MPTP mice, and Mima 2020 (PMC7071483) improved Barnes-maze spatial memory in SAMP8 mice, Zargar-Nattaj et al. 2011 (PMC3218779) reported mixed offspring passive-avoidance results (worse at 1 h, better at 24 h-1 wk). Critically, none of these human or animal studies administered dedicated attention or executive-function tests (attention impairment; outcome_fit: remote), and leaf-extract memory studies (Mani 2011) are excluded.

Opposing preclinical PD-model evidence leans against the claim that toasted coriander seed worsens bradykinesia: Koppula et al. 2021 (local PMC8222636, PMID:34177406; n=60 Swiss albino mice, 10/group) demonstrated that 21 days of oral Coriandrum sativum fruit (seed) extract (100, 200, 300 mg/kg p.o.) in MPTP+probenecid Parkinsonian mice significantly restored day-21 open-field line crossings, rearing, and grooming and reduced immobility time (P<0.05 to P<0.001; non-sedating in seed-only 300 mg/kg controls), while Mohan et al. 2015 (local extract, PMID:26040026) found oral ethanolic coriander seed extract (100-200 mg/kg p.o. x 15 d) increased locomotion (P<0.05) in tacrine-treated rats. Zhang 2015 bridges roasting retention. Important caveats preserved: acute intraperitoneal aqueous seed extract in healthy mice reduced spontaneous activity (Emamghoreishi 2005, route-dependent sedation), and leaf-extract PD rodent studies (Lee 2026; Saeki 2022) tested cilantro leaves rather than seeds and are excluded. Animal extract models and zero human PD motor trials cap certainty at minimal_signal (50.005).

Because evidence rests on a single rodent PD model using seed extract (not human PD postural pull-test or posturography trials with ground culinary seed), certainty is minimal_signal (50.005).
